summary: A family field that was made hekdesh can be bought back. The price depends on how many years are left until Yovel.

chunks.he: אֵין מַקְדִּישִׁין לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.
chunks.en: A family field may not be made hekdesh less than two years before Yovel,
chunks.st: One may neither consecrate an ancestral field, i.e., a field that he inherited, less than two years before the Jubilee Year,

words.note: The fiftieth year, when fields go back to their families.

chunks.he: וְלֹא גוֹאֲלִין לְאַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁנָה.
chunks.en: and it may not be bought back less than one year after Yovel.
chunks.st: nor may one redeem such a field less than one year after the Jubilee Year.
chunks.stMore: When redeeming an ancestral field that has been consecrated, the sum paid to redeem the field is calculated based on the number of years remaining until the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: We do not count months to help the person against hekdesh;
chunks.explain: He pays for the whole year.
chunks.st: When performing this calculation, one does not count months of a partial year in order to lower the price to be paid to the Temple treasury;
chunks.stMore: rather, he pays for the entire year.

chunks.en: but hekdesh does count months.
chunks.st: But the Temple treasury may count months
chunks.stMore: in order to raise the price of redemption, as will be explained.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his field hekdesh at a time when Yovel is kept,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates his ancestral field during a period when the Jubilee Year is observed

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן בְּזֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעֹרִים חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף.
chunks.en: gives fifty silver shekels for each area big enough to plant a chomer of barley.
chunks.explain: A chomer is a big measure of seeds.
chunks.st: he gives the Temple treasury fifty sela, a talmudic measure referred to in the Bible as silver shekels, for an area required for sowing a ḥomer, a measure known in talmudic terminology as one kor, of barley seed (see Leviticus 27:16).

chunks.he: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמֻקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
chunks.en: If there were ditches ten tefachim deep,
chunks.st: If there were crevices [neka’im] ten handbreadths deep in the field,

words.note: A tefach is about the width of a hand.

chunks.en: or rocks ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: or if there were boulders ten handbreadths high,

chunks.en: they are not measured with the field.
chunks.st: then when calculating the redemption price those areas are not measured with the rest of the field.

chunks.en: If they were less than that,
chunks.st: But if the depth of the crevices, or the height of the boulders, was less than that amount,

chunks.en: they are measured with the field.
chunks.st: they are measured with the rest of the field.

chunks.en: If he made it hekdesh two or three
chunks.st: If he consecrated the field two or three

chunks.en: years before Yovel,
chunks.st: years before the Jubilee Year and wishes to redeem it,

chunks.en: he gives a sela and a pundyon for each year.
chunks.explain: A pundyon is a small coin.
chunks.st: he gives the Temple treasury a sela and a pundeyon, a pundeyon being one forty-eighth of a sela, per year

chunks.en: If he said, "I will give
chunks.st: And if he said: I will give

chunks.en: each year's money in that year,"
chunks.st: the payment for each year during that year,

chunks.en: we do not listen to him;
chunks.st: one does not listen to him;

chunks.en: rather, he gives all of it at once.
chunks.st: rather, he must give the entire sum in one payment.

summary: Anyone may buy back a field from hekdesh. But the owner adds a fifth.

chunks.en: It is the same for the owner
chunks.st: This is the halakha both with regard to a case where the owner redeems the field

chunks.en: and for any other person.
chunks.st: and a case where any other person redeems the field.

chunks.he: מַה בֵּין הַבְּעָלִים לְבֵין כָּל הָאָדָם,
chunks.en: What is the difference between the owner and any other person?
chunks.st: What then is the difference between redemption by the owner and redemption by any other person?

chunks.en: Only that the owner adds a fifth,
chunks.st: It is only that the owner gives an extra one-fifth in addition to the payment,

chunks.en: and any other person does not add a fifth.
chunks.st: and any other person who redeems the field does not give the additional one-fifth.

summary: What happens at Yovel to a family field that was made hekdesh, depending on who bought it back.

chunks.en: If he made it hekdesh and he himself bought it back,
chunks.st: If one consecrated his ancestral field and then redeemed it himself,

chunks.en: it does not leave his hands at Yovel.
chunks.st: it is not removed from his possession to be divided among the priests during the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: If his son bought it back,
chunks.st: If his son redeemed it,

chunks.en: it goes back to his father at Yovel.
chunks.st: the field is removed from the son’s possession and returns to his father during the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: If someone else, or one
chunks.st: But if another person or one of his

chunks.en: of the relatives, bought it back, and he bought it back from that person,
chunks.st: other relatives redeemed the field and the owner subsequently redeemed it from his possession,

chunks.en: it does not leave his hands at Yovel.
chunks.explain: Steinsaltz has a different version here: the field goes to the Kohanim at Yovel.
chunks.st: the field is removed from the owner’s possession and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: If one of the Kohanim bought it back,
chunks.st: If one of the priests redeemed the field

chunks.en: and at Yovel it is in his hands,
chunks.st: and when the Jubilee arrived it was in his possession,

chunks.he: לֹא יֹאמַר הוֹאִיל וְהִיא יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים
chunks.en: he may not say, "Since it goes to the Kohanim
chunks.st: he may not say: Since it is removed from the possession of the one who redeemed it and given to the priests

chunks.en: at Yovel, and it is in my hands,
chunks.st: during the Jubilee Year, and since it is already in my possession,

chunks.en: it is mine."
chunks.st: it is mine.

chunks.en: Rather, it goes out to all his brothers the Kohanim.
chunks.st: Rather, the field is removed from his possession and is divided among all his brethren, the priests.

summary: What happens to a field that was made hekdesh if nobody bought it back before Yovel? The Tannaim argue.

chunks.en: If Yovel came and the field was not bought back,
chunks.st: If one consecrated his ancestral field and the Jubilee Year arrived and it was not redeemed by the owner or anyone else,

chunks.he: הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִים לְתוֹכָהּ וְנוֹתְנִים אֶת דָּמֶיהָ,
chunks.en: the Kohanim go into it and pay its price to hekdesh,
chunks.st: the priests enter into the field and give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

words.note: A great Tanna of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: they go into it, but they do not pay.
chunks.st: They enter into the field, but they do not give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: they do not go into it and they do not pay.
chunks.st: The priests do not enter into the field, and they also do not give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: Rather, it is called a left-alone field,
chunks.st: Rather, the field remains in the possession of the Temple treasury, and it is called: An abandoned field,

chunks.en: until the second Yovel.
chunks.st: until the second Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: If the second Yovel came and it was not bought back,
chunks.st: If the second Jubilee arrived and it was still not redeemed,

chunks.he: נִקְרֵאת רְטוּשֵׁי רְטוּשִׁין עַד הַיּוֹבֵל הַשְּׁלִישִׁי.
chunks.en: it is called a field left alone twice, until the third Yovel.
chunks.st: it is called: An abandoned field from among the abandoned fields, meaning one that was abandoned twice, until the third Jubilee.

chunks.en: The Kohanim never go into it,
chunks.st: In any case, the priests never enter into a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year

chunks.en: until someone else buys it back.
chunks.st: until another person redeems it first.

summary: A field that a son bought from his father: does it count as his own family field or as a bought field? Also, Kohanim and Levi'im can make their fields hekdesh and buy them back at any time.

chunks.en: Someone who bought a field from his father,
chunks.st: One who purchases an ancestral field from his father,

chunks.en: and his father died, and afterward he made it hekdesh,
chunks.st: and his father subsequently died and afterward the son consecrated it,

chunks.en: it is like a family field.
chunks.st: its halakhic status is like that of an ancestral field,
chunks.stMore: as he inherited his father’s ancestral rights prior to the consecration. Consequently, the field’s redemption price is calculated on the basis of fifty sela per beit kor, and if another redeems it instead of the son, it is given to the priests during the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: If he made it hekdesh, and afterward his father died,
chunks.st: But if the son consecrated the field and afterward his father died,

chunks.en: it is like a field that was bought,
chunks.st: its halakhic status is like that of a purchased field,
chunks.stMore: whose redemption price is based on its monetary value, and which will return to the ancestral owner, i.e., the son, at the Jubilee;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:

chunks.en: it is like a family field,
chunks.st: Even in a case where the son consecrated the field before his father died, its halakhic status is like that of an ancestral field,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 27),
chunks.st: as it is stated
chunks.stMore: with regard to a purchased field: “And if he will consecrate unto the Lord

chunks.en: "And if a field that he bought,
chunks.st: a field that he has bought,

chunks.en: which is not from his family's field,"
chunks.st: which is not of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:22),

chunks.he: שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּה,
chunks.en: this means a field that will not become his family field.
chunks.st: indicating that this halakha applies only to a field that is not due to become his ancestral field,

chunks.en: That leaves out this field,
chunks.st: thereby excluding this field,

chunks.en: which will become his family field.
chunks.explain: It will be his when his father dies.
chunks.st: which at the time of consecration is due to become his ancestral field in the future, when his father dies.

chunks.he: שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל,
chunks.en: A bought field does not go to the Kohanim at Yovel,
chunks.st: The mishna continues: A purchased field that was consecrated is not removed from the possession of the Temple treasury and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ.
chunks.en: because a person cannot make hekdesh something that is not his.
chunks.st: as the purchase of the land was valid only until the Jubilee, at which point fields return to their ancestral owners, and a person cannot consecrate an item that is not his.

chunks.en: Kohanim and Levi'im may make their fields hekdesh at any time,
chunks.st: The priests and the Levites may always consecrate their ancestral fields

chunks.en: and buy them back at any time,
chunks.st: and may always redeem their ancestral fields,

chunks.en: whether before Yovel
chunks.st: both before the Jubilee Year

chunks.en: or after Yovel.
chunks.st: and after the Jubilee Year.
